title: Fidelity-drop fallback + prefetch snapshot protocol for OOM avoidance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a multi-tier runtime protocol that prevents and recovers from GPU OOMs by preferring graceful fidelity degradation and prefetchable KV snapshots before resorting to model fallbacks or request retries. This ticket defines the admission and runtime behavior for continuous-batching paths, KV snapshot prefetching, and the fidelity-drop decision graph to preserve latency SLOs while avoiding hard OOM failures.
background: Recent production incidents show that large prefix-heavy requests combined with aggressive batching and long-lived KV caches cause transient GPU OOMs on high-occupancy hosts. Existing mitigations (eviction and hard model fallback) either cause large quality regressions or long tails on latency. We need a lighter-weight intermediate path that maintains most user-facing quality while preventing OOMs and keeping failover predictable for caller applications.
proposed_solution: Protocol summary: 1) Proactive occupancy scoring: at admission, compute a per-request occupancy score derived from prefix length, kv_cache_size_estimate, expected generation tokens, and current host free-memory watermark. 2) Prefetchable KV snapshots: introduce small async snapshots of a request's KV into pinned host memory (or compressed host store) when occupancy score exceeds threshold T_prefetch to allow quick spill-and-restore. 3) Fidelity-drop phase: on memory pressure or pre-admission when occupancy > T_fidelity, dynamically apply a fidelity profile that (a) caps max generation length, (b) switches to low-memory attention kernel (memory-slim attention), and/or (c) enables lossy KV compression (blockwise quantize to 4-bit with fast decode in kernel). Fidelity profiles are parameterized so we can A/B multiple levels. 4) Degrade admission window: if fidelity profile used, shrink batch admission window to favor latency (reduce batch wait) and mark request as degraded in tracing. 5) Async CPU offload: if fidelity+prefetch still insufficient and host triggers OOM sentinel, spill non-hot KV pages to host memory using prefetch snapshots to allow quick partial restore; schedule an async restore when memory pressure subsides. 6) Controlled model fallback: as final step, route to a smaller model variant only for degraded requests after a bounded retry/backoff (to preserve SLA). 7) Observability & indicators: emit structured events for fidelity changes, spill/restore operations, snapshot usage, and fallback routing so Console can surface regressions. The implementation will be gated behind a runtime flag and rollout via canary with per-customer controls.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce host-level hard OOM incidents by >= 60% in canary pool compared to baseline within 2 weeks
For requests that use fidelity-drop: median latency increase <= 10% and p95 increase <= 25% relative to non-degraded baseline
Quality regression for fidelity-drop requests measured by existing eval suite: average BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop <= 6% for target prompt sets
Snapshots enable spill/restore and reduce fallback-to-smaller-model events by >= 40%
All fidelity transitions, spill, and fallback events are visible in Console traces and generate alerts when OOM sentinel fires
notes: Trade-offs: fidelity-drop preserves availability but introduces quality variance; need explicit telemetry to link customer-visible errors to fidelity changes
KV snapshot storage must be bounded per-request — implement LRU for snapshot cache and a size cap per GPU host to avoid swapping the problem to host memory
Continuous batching: when a request is marked for fidelity-degrade, it should bypass long batching windows to avoid compounded memory pressure from other queued requests
Performance knobs: thresholds T_prefetch and T_fidelity are workload-dependent; include autotune job to suggest defaults per model-profile
Security: snapshots remain encrypted at rest with KMS keys; snapshot REST endpoints are internal-only and short-lived
